root_cause.summary: Zendesk AI Gateway sits behind an istio-envoy mesh that returns 403 RBAC:access denied to ANY request arriving via the OpenShell L7 MITM proxy — including a bare GET with NO credential header. Host direct calls succeed (200) with the same key, same URL, same headers, on BOTH HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2.
discriminators: HOST direct POST /anthropic/v1/messages x-api-key=real -> 200 (real model response)
HOST direct, --http1.1 -> 200 ; --http2 -> 200  (HTTP version NOT the cause)
HOST direct, x-api-key AND Authorization:Bearer -> both 200 (header form NOT the cause)
SANDBOX via OpenShell proxy, x-api-key=placeholder -> 403 istio-envoy RBAC
SANDBOX via proxy, bare GET / with NO credential -> 403 istio-envoy RBAC (proves credential is irrelevant; the mesh rejects the PROXY's connection)
Supervisor log: ALLOWED POST .../anthropic/v1/messages [policy:model_ai_gateway engine:l7] — OpenShell allowed+forwarded it; the 403 is from istio-envoy UPSTREAM
No client-cert/mTLS required (server requests none; host handshake clean)
OpenShell endpoint enforcement modes: only enforce/audit; NO tls-passthrough mode that would preserve the client's TLS identity to the gateway
root_cause.conclusion: The Zendesk AI Gateway's istio RBAC does not authorize connections that arrive through the OpenShell L7 MITM proxy (the proxy re-originates the TLS connection with its own identity). OpenShell's credential-injection model REQUIRES L7 MITM to rewrite the placeholder. These two are in direct conflict for this gateway. The host's working path has no proxy.

impact: R-U1-6 GATE (AI Gateway track) cannot be proven via OpenShell credential injection against ai-gateway.zende.sk as currently deployed.
options: A) Infra fix: configure the AI Gateway's istio RBAC to authorize the OpenShell proxy's egress (identity/CIDR/SA). Likely needs Zendesk platform team — external dependency.

B) OpenShell TLS-passthrough for this endpoint: allow the agent's own TLS (with its identity) to reach the gateway so mesh RBAC passes. But then the L7 placeholder rewrite cannot happen — breaks the injection model (contradiction).
C) Bypass model: run the model call with the REAL key in-sandbox (not the placeholder), violating R-X-5 'no creds on disk' — NOT acceptable per constraints.
D) NO-GO on the AI Gateway track for Phase 1; document as the de-risk finding; revisit when the gateway admits proxied traffic. Falls to operator decision per R-X-4.
